answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable onyx stake that is locked for the whole epoch. A newcomer starts on a small island of low-trust work: only cheap, verifiable tasks with tiny payouts, so a fake identity earns almost nothing. Sustained honest work gradually raises its stake and reputation toward the summit, where high-value jobs unlock. Creating thousands of fake agents would demand a separate stake per identity plus weeks of low-paid labor each, making the attack cost far more than any reward it could extract.
